problem: Existing CoIN benchmarks entangle question-asking with navigation policy, need slow full simulator episodes, are non-reproducible because the simulated human answers vary per run, and use low-quality (hallucinated) LLaVA-generated target descriptions.
motivation: Human-agent collaboration is needed to disambiguate visually similar instances, but without a disentangled, fast and reproducible evaluation one cannot measure interaction reasoning itself. Prior methods (AIUTA) add heavy modular LLM/VLM pipelines with high latency, and there was no training data for interaction reasoning.
key_idea: Build QAsk-NAV, a benchmark with a navigation-independent question-asking protocol (questioner vs. oracle over synthesized distractor images), improved navigation descriptions and a 28k reasoning/question trace dataset, and use it to fine-tune a single small VLM (7B) that replaces modular pipelines.
insight: Targeted supervision on reasoning traces with uncertainty scores lets a 7B model beat a 20B modular system and a 30B VLM at question asking, indicating that scale/modularity is not required. The first-stage ablation (MAE on scores) shows that producing reasoning plus score beats score-only, both fine-tuned and base. Description-type analysis shows QAsk-NAV-agent improves monotonically with description specificity while AIUTA does not, and better annotations raise SR of both methods by roughly 1.3x, showing annotation quality strongly affects navigation results.
method: Question-asking protocol: a questioner sees the target description D and a sequence of distractor images ending with the target; at each step it asks a question or gives a binary match decision, while an oracle VLM with the target image answers; scored by SR, FR, NQ, Time, averaged over 3 oracles.

Distractor synthesis: Gemini-3-pro-image edits base images (color, salient feature, context; 5 variants of 10 base images per category) to make fine-grained distractors; six description levels (category ... color-context-feature); ~1400 episodes (~1000 train/~400 test).

Navigation protocol: CoIN-Bench episodes (1,649: 831/359/459 for val seen/synonyms/unseen) with Gemini-3-pro regenerated descriptions (shorter, 9.66 words) and Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B as the oracle in Habitat.

QAsk-NAV dataset: ~28k tuples (D,O,R,S,Q,C) with reasoning, uncertainty score S in {0,1,2} and question; ~24k from Gemini-3-pro annotation plus ~4k rollouts of Gemini-3-flash questioner/oracle; splits 15.98k/6.38k/5.03k.

Agent architecture: Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct on top of a VLFM navigation policy; when a same-category object is detected, outputs (R,S,Q); S=2 accepts as candidate, S=0 discards, S=1 asks and adds Q/A to context.
Two-stage training: SFT on reasoning+score samples without questions/context, then SFT on question samples with non-empty context mixed with non-question samples at 10:1.

setting.backbone: Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct (fine-tuned) as interaction module + VLFM (zero-shot modular) navigation policy
setting.training_data: QAsk-NAV dataset train split (15.98k reasoning/question traces generated by Gemini-3-pro and Gemini-3-flash rollouts)
setting.observation: egocentric RGB (512x512) with depth for VLFM; natural-language dialogue
setting.action_space: low-level Forward 0.25m, Turn Left/Right 15°, Stop, Ask
setting.privileged: none for the agent (oracle VLM sees target image only for answering questions in evaluation)

numbers.extra: new Gemini-3-pro annotations; Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B oracle; 500 steps, 0.25m success radius
Val Seen Synonyms split; new annotations
metrics averaged over Gemini-2.5-pro, Gemini-3-flash, Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B oracles

numbers_note: Question-asking values printed as fractions; converted to percent for SR/FR. NQ and Time are as printed (0.1990, 1.15).
results: On the question-asking protocol the 7B agent gets SR 0.4510 / FR 0.3317, beating AIUTA° (0.3027/0.1993, 20B, 177.83s) and Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B (0.3205/0.2755), while being far faster; Gemini-3-flash remains much higher (0.9329). In navigation it beats AIUTA on Val Seen (SR 12.20 vs 10.46) and Val Unseen (9.63 vs 7.83), but is below AIUTA on Val Seen Synonyms (14.15 vs 14.89) and OVON (15.88).
limitations: Performs poorly on the least informative category-only descriptions (SR 0.06), preferring to act rather than ask; large gap to Gemini-3-flash.
Absolute navigation SR remains low (~10-14%) and depends on VLFM detector/policy; oracle is a VLM and the descriptions/data are synthetic (Gemini-generated).
Question-asking metrics for AIUTA° use a replaced Qwen3-13B LLM, so it is not the original system.
